title: SNP-distance thresholds are decision rules
dek: A 5-SNP or 12-SNP cutoff to call “recent transmission” is a screen, not P(who infected whom). The clock, the mask, within-host diversity, and missing cases all sit between a count and an edge.
story: Pairwise SNP distance on a core alignment is a useful integer. It is not a likelihood of a directed transmission event. A threshold — 5 SNPs for “recent,” 12 for a looser cluster — is a decision rule with a false-near and false-far rate that depends on the clock, the mask, mixed infection, and how much of the outbreak you sequenced.

Published MTBC clocks are typically a fraction of a SNP per genome per year on a masked core, with wide intervals and lineage heterogeneity. Several SNPs can accumulate within a host before diagnosis. A 0-SNP pair can still be two people infected by an unsampled third. A 6-SNP pair can be household transmission plus a mask difference.

The stats transmission-genomics plate is the full caveat list. This plate is the beginner object: what the integer is, why people pick 5, and why a methods section that omits the mask is not a distance.
deepTitle: How to quote a distance without lying
deep: Always: reference build, mask (PE/PPE, repeats, often DR genes if you do not want treatment to look like phylogeny), mapping quality, mixed-site handling.
Homoplasy in resistance genes inflates unmasked distances among unrelated RR-TB. Masking DR genes can hide true within-host evolution under treatment. Say which you did.
Cluster definition (single-linkage at threshold t) is not a tree. Two isolates 4 SNPs from a third and 9 from each other can join one cluster at t = 5 via the third.
Dated trees and structured coalescents are models. Thresholds are screens to choose pairs for those models, or for epi follow-up.

example.title: 4 SNPs unmasked, 1 SNP masked
example.setup: Two household isolates. Unmasked distance 4, of which 3 SNPs sit in PE_PGRS. Core-masked distance 1. A slide titles this “below the 5-SNP threshold, proven transmission.”

steps.title: The integer moved with the mask
steps.body: Without the mask, you were counting mapping noise as phylogeny. With the mask, d = 1 is compatible with household transmission and with a shared source. It is not a directed edge.

steps.title: Threshold as screen
steps.body: d = 1 passes a 5-SNP screen for follow-up. Proven means epi plus genomics plus (ideally) a model. The screen is the start.

steps.title: Report both if PE SNPs were the story
steps.body: If someone wants to argue PE diversity, that is a different, harder alignment. Do not mix it into the transmission integer silently.

example.takeaway: A threshold cuts overlapping densities. Name the mask or you did not have a distance.

check.prompt: A 5-SNP cutoff for “recent transmission” is best described as:
choices: A decision rule / screen whose error rates depend on clock, mask, and sampling
A Bayes factor that does not need a clock
check.answer: A decision rule / screen whose error rates depend on clock, mask, and sampling
check.why: Thresholds are not likelihoods of who infected whom.

whyWrong.P(directed transmission | data) = 1: Distance is not a posterior edge.
whyWrong.A Bayes factor that does not need a cloc: A BF would need models; a cutoff is not that.

check.prompt: Unmasked d = 12, of which 10 SNPs are in PE/PPE. Masked core d = 2. For a 5-SNP recent-transmission screen you should quote:
choices: 12, because more SNPs are more conservative
The masked distance (2), with the mask named — 12 was inflated by poorly mapped genes
check.answer: The masked distance (2), with the mask named — 12 was inflated by poorly mapped genes
check.why: PE/PPE SNPs are the classic inflation. The screen uses the core integer you defined.

check.prompt: On the density plate, the 5-SNP idea is a cut through overlapping curves. That picture warns that:
check.figureHint: Household, outbreak, and far-lineage mounds overlap.
choices: Thresholds perfectly separate household from non-recent pairs with no errors
False-near and false-far pairs exist because the clouds overlap; the cut is a screen
check.answer: False-near and false-far pairs exist because the clouds overlap; the cut is a screen
check.why: Overlapping densities are why a cutoff is not a posterior.
